main_text.p: mus nostro sæculo vir doctrinâ & pietate clarus Iacobus Bifrons, Rhætus, hanc linguam scriptis illustrare & publicare incœpit, qui catechismum etiam sacrosanctæ religionis nostræ è Germanico in hunc sermonem convertit, excusum Pusclavii, anno salutis 1552.
main_text.head: Oratio Dominica in vernaculo Rhætorum sermone, quem ipsi vulgò Romanum appellant, (ut & suum Sabaudi,) nostri Churwælsch.
main_text.p: Bap noass, tîi quell chi ésch in ls tschéls: fatt saingk ùènnga ilg teis nuom: ilg teis ragin am uéng naun proa: la tia uœllga dwain tafchkoa in tschél, ufchè eir in terra. Noass paun d' minchiady daa a nuo hoátz:e pardunaa nuo ils noas dabitts, schkoa eir, nuo pardunain a ls noass dabittaduors. E nun ns' manar in prowamaint, moa ans spendra da lg maal. Parchiai chia teis ais ilg raginam è la pussaunt za, è lg laud,in etern. Amen.

Rhæti non à Romanis, ut vulgò putant, sed à Tuscis originem traxêre. Hos Livius nihil scribit ex antiquo præter sonum linguæ,nec eum incorruptum retinuisse. Cæsterùm Rhætica lingua,ut auctor est Ægidius Tschudus,intra centum quinquaginta annos plurimùm apud Rhætos interiit, GermanicaRhæti orti seno Romani, sed à Tuscis.

page.notes: Left margin note is written in italic black type and reads as printed in the scan; its letters are partly obscured. Word-level readings of the Romansh passage are uncertain in several places and were transcribed as printed; no [?] markers were added to avoid guessing. The final word "Germanica" continues on the next page, so the last paragraph ends at the page foot as printed.
